messages:
ria (eng-runtime): Heads-up — I ran the microcoalesce sweep on staging this morning. Dropped micro-batch interval from 6ms -> 3ms, coalesce_delay=1ms, jitter=uniform(0,2ms). Kernel v2.4.1 pinned. Observed 10-12% throughput uptick but p95/p99 latency increased on chat workloads when KV hit-rate < 60%.

sam: Nice. Do you have flamegraphs or traces?

ria (eng-runtime): Pasted a short CPU flame excerpt and a tiny trace: 
```
# perf top snapshot (abridged)
llama_attention_kernel  45%
kv_cache_lookup        18%
scheduler_lock         8%
memcpy                 6%
others                 23%
```
Trace: saw tail queuing in scheduler where short coalesce windows produced many tiny batches, increasing kernel startup overhead per token.

lee: Did you try increasing token_budget per-batch? Might amortize kernel init.

ria (eng-runtime): Yup — bumping token_budget from 256->512 reduced p99 by ~7ms in local sim, but on staging we still see kv_cache thrash: hit-rate drops due to more frequent context swaps.

carol: Could this be a regression introduced by kernel v2.4.1? It changed kernel tiling heuristics, might be worse for very small batches.

perf-bot: deploy v2.4.1 to staging at 2026-03-12T09:12:00Z (marker)

sam: If kernel startup overhead dominates for small batches, we should consider adaptive coalesce: increase coalesce_delay if batch size < threshold OR if kv_hit_rate < 70%.

ria (eng-runtime): Proposal sketch: 
```json
{
  "micro_batch_interval_ms": 3,
  "coalesce_delay_ms": "adaptive", 
  "coalesce_policy": {
    "min_batch_size": 8,
    "token_budget_target": 400,
    "jitter_ms": "uniform(0,2)"
  },
  "kv_feedback": {
    "kv_hit_rate_threshold": 0.7,
    "increase_delay_ms": 2
  }
}
```
This would defer small batches slightly when KV hit-rate is low and target more tokens per batch when kernel variant shows high startup overhead.

lee: Sounds reasonable. Any perf regress tests to validate? We should run A/B with 1h traffic replay and monitor p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, kernel_cpu%.

carol: Also add a canary that pins kernel to v2.3.x for comparison — if v2.3 beats v2.4.1 on tail under small-window regimes then file a kernel rollback.

ria (eng-runtime): Agreed. Action items: 1) run 1h replay with adaptive coalesce config vs fixed baseline (me) 2) run kernel A/B v2.3.x vs v2.4.1 w/ same config (carol) 3) add metric alert for kv_hit_rate drop >10% (sam)

sam: I'll own the alert. Quick note — add a short histogram for batch_token_count; it helped earlier to catch mode-splitting.

ria (eng-runtime): Will share experiment run IDs soon. TL;DR: small coalesce windows + kernel tiling changes amplify startup overhead; adaptive delay + token-budget targets look promising to trade a few ms for better p99 when KV cache isn't helping. :chart_with_upwards_trend: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

carol: Thanks — ping me when runs finish, we can decide rollout/rollback cadence. :thumbsup:
